SMTO-WEB-0052 — The link didn't return a real PDF

GUID: 06643c27-124d-56dc-85b1-6214fe775ed1
Slug: web-document-type-mismatch
Domain: WEB · Subsystem: web_research

What happened

  • SMTO expected a PDF, but what the website sent isn't a PDF file. It's often a web page, a sign-in page or an error page instead. SMTO didn't save it.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the link in your own web browser and see whether it downloads a PDF or shows a web page. Many sites show a sign-in, cookie or error page instead of the file when visited automatically.
  2. If you find the direct download link for the PDF, send it to SMTO in a new message. A link that serves the file itself lets SMTO download and read it.
  3. If the PDF is behind a sign-in, download it yourself and attach it to your message. SMTO can read a file you attach even when the site won't hand it over automatically.

What success looks like

  • SMTO reports that the PDF was downloaded and can read its pages.

If it still fails

  • If a link that opens as a PDF in your browser still fails, select Copy error details and send them, with the link, to the person who manages SMTO.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • PDF acquisition rejected the response because its decoded bytes do not begin with a supported PDF signature (%PDF-1.x or %PDF-2.x), regardless of the URL or filename.

What this means

  • Acquired document bytes do not start with a supported PDF version signature. The diagnostic adds no retrieval. Read outcomes and retained receipts determine what evidence is available; an error does not establish the content of an unread source.

Why this can happen

  • Acquired document bytes do not start with a supported PDF version signature.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the recorded type/signature failure without treating a renamed file as valid PDF evidence.

How to fix it

  • web/documents.acquire() requires the first 8 decoded bytes to match %PDF-[12].N; a body that ends before the signature or starts with anything else fails with document_type_mismatch. Point the request at a URL that serves real PDF bytes (application/pdf or application/octet-stream); a .pdf filename is not proof of type, and a renamed non-PDF must not be treated as a validated PDF.
  • Use a source returning a PDF signature and PDF or generic binary content type. A filename is not type evidence.

Retry and execution caution

  • Use verified facts or an explicit scoped limitation.

How to verify the fix

  • The source returns a supported PDF representation and later extraction succeeds.

What not to do

  • Do not rename a non-PDF response and treat it as a validated PDF.

Technical notes

  • The diagnostic adds no retrieval. Read outcomes and retained receipts determine what evidence is available; an error does not establish the content of an unread source.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
